| Scene description | • The site is a grey-paved pedestrian area in Xinjiali Fashion Plaza, Jianghan District, with shared bicycles and electric scooters parked nearby.<br>• S13-A-01 and S13-A-02 show black mesh-sided bins with ‘Recyclables’ and ‘Residual waste’ openings, without obvious overflow. In S13-A-02, a torn beige woven sack lies beside the bin and cigarette ends and other items rest on top.<br>• S13-A-03 shows a construction area with grey stone blocks, red-blue-white striped sacks, scattered waste and some standing water, forming clear accumulation.<br>• In S13-A-05, a red firefighting sandbag labelled ‘Incity’ stands beside a yellow barrier and parked scooters, without obvious bins or accumulation on the ground. Overall, bins do not overflow, but accumulations occur around the construction area and bins. |
| Regulatory basis | • Commercial and public-space managers, such as property managers or shopping-centre operators, should maintain daily sanitation, timely collection, functional classification facilities and freedom from accumulation. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 12.<br>• Littering or stockpiling waste in public spaces and dumping, scattering or stockpiling outside designated areas are prohibited. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 17.<br>• Classification containers should be clean, intact and free of overflow, with no litter nearby, meeting disposal-point sanitation requirements. Signs for classification of municipal solid waste.<br>• Construction areas should provide temporary collection points, classify and promptly remove waste, and avoid impacts on public spaces. Standard for Environment and Sanitation at Construction Sites (JGJ 147-2016), Section 5.3.2.<br>• Responsible organisations failing to clear waste and causing sanitation problems may receive warnings or fines, or suspension for rectification in serious cases, where management duties are unfulfilled. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 36. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Four accumulations include substantial construction-area waste and standing water, creating potential insect and pollution risks. Litter beside bins impairs appearance, although no overflow, severe pollution or public-safety threat is evident. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects: construction waste and standing water present sanitation risks, while litter beside bins reduces pedestrian-area cleanliness. Near-term risks: delayed clearance may encourage insects and odours, affect businesses and pedestrians, create slippery waterlogged areas during rain, and allow unsorted construction waste to pollute soil or water. |
| Potential causes | • Construction accumulation may reflect absent temporary collection points or delayed removal: stones, sacks and litter lie without an obvious container.<br>• Litter beside bins may reflect public behaviour or insufficient cleaning: S13-A-02 has cigarettes on top and a torn sack on the ground.<br>• Accumulation in areas without bins may reflect absent, hidden or moved facilities: S13-A-05 has scooters but no bin and may be temporary parking or a management blind spot.<br>• Verify collection records, construction responsibilities and bin layout plans, and observe cleaning and classification signs. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could worsen sanitation and make the commercial area less attractive. Prolonged construction-waste storage may pollute soil or groundwater; uncleared litter may present fire risks, for example from cigarettes igniting combustibles. Regulatory penalties may also affect managers’ credit ratings. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: clear S13-A-03 waste and standing water and add temporary barriers or warnings; clear litter around S13-A-02 and inspect bin condition; provide temporary bins or guidance at S13-A-05.<br>• Longer-term action: assign construction-waste responsibilities and routine checks; increase or reposition bins at scooter parking and construction areas; promote classification and supervision; and establish cleaning checks, feedback and corrective action. |
| Priority | **Medium.** Four accumulations, particularly in the construction area, impair appearance and sanitation without severe pollution or an urgent public-safety incident. Address soon to prevent escalation. |
